Shield agrees to acquire Echodyne for up to $5.3 billion

The radar acquisition is expected to close in early 2027, subject to conditions, with standalone MESA products retained.

Echodyne ↗5 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Transaction terms

Shield agreed to acquire Echodyne for up to $5.3 billion: $4.8 billion at closing and up to $500 million tied to performance conditions. Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to approvals and other conditions. The acquisition is not yet complete.

Sensing technology

Echodyne makes compact solid-state radars using MESA technology for detection and tracking. Civilian applications include airports, stadiums and airspace management for police or fire services. Linking sensing with autonomy is central to the deal, but the announcement is not a new system-performance test.

Products and manufacturing

The companies intend to retain Echodyne’s team and standalone MESA radar sales after closing. A new 86,350-square-foot facility, representing a $40 million investment, is designed for about 30,000 radars annually. That describes intended capacity, not completed production or shipments.
